source_text: Ac per hoc necessarie interrogavi, quid suum cognosceret diabolus in sexibus, per quod fructum eorum iure decerperet; qui nec carnem compegerat, nec membra formaverat, nec genitalia dederat, nec distinxerat sexum, nec coniugium ordinaverat, nec commixtionem, sine qua coniugium esse non potest, aut fecunditate honoraverat, aut voluptate resperserat.
pass_a_gloss: And through this I necessarily asked what the devil would recognize as his own in the sexes, through which he would pluck their fruit by right; who had neither fitted the flesh together, nor formed the members, nor given the genitals, nor distinguished sex, nor ordained marriage, nor had either honored with fertility or sprinkled with pleasure the mingling, without which marriage cannot be.

lemmas.lexica: LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice

pass_b_english: I therefore had to ask what the devil recognized as his own in the sexes, by which he could rightfully pluck their fruit. He had not assembled the flesh, formed the members, given the reproductive organs, distinguished sex, or ordained marriage. Nor had he honored with fertility or sprinkled with pleasure the union without which marriage cannot exist.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Julian contrasts opportunity/help with imposed necessity; load-bearing against natural compulsion to sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
